intended_object: The canonical map T(M) ⊗_R T(N) → ∏_{p,q} M^{⊗p} ⊗_R N^{⊗q}. It sends an algebraic tensor of finite tensor words to its family of bidegree components, i.e. it includes the algebraic tensor product into the completed tensor square. This is inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
`TensorWords R M` is the direct sum ⨁ₙ M^{⊗n}, and `TensorWords.component R M p` is the projection onto its degree-p summand. Here `TensorProduct R M N` is not Mathlib's tensor product: it is the local abbrev ∀ p q, M^{⊗p} ⊗ N^{⊗q}, the product over bidegrees.

The definition sends z to the family whose (p, q) entry is (π_p ⊗ π_q)(z). Since T(M) ⊗ T(N) ≅ ⨁_{p,q} M^{⊗p} ⊗ N^{⊗q}, this map is the direct sum followed by the canonical map from a direct sum into the product. That is the intended inclusion into the bidegree completion.

The definition only assumes a commutative semiring R and modules over it, which is the natural generality. Mathlib has no completed tensor algebra, so there is no Mathlib counterpart for this map into the bidegree product.
